_comment: How each official SDK is driven by the conformance harness, and which canonical
`export` runs in the SDK's own directory with two environment variables set:
FRAISEQL_CONFORMANCE_OUT      absolute path to write schema.json to
It must author the fixture through the SDK's PUBLIC authoring API — never by
hand-assembling the expected JSON. Six of the eleven pre-existing parity generators
did exactly that and were therefore incapable of failing.
`unsupported` maps a construct name to the reason the SDK cannot author it. The
default is that every construct is required: adding one to project.CONSTRUCTS fails
every SDK until each either implements it or declares the gap here. Declaring a gap
is deliberate and public — README.md renders these reasons into the support matrix.
A declaration that is no longer true also fails, so the matrix cannot go stale.

unsupported.fact_tables: the SDK has no fact-table authoring surface — its only `fact_table` matches are the mutation key `invalidates_fact_tables` (AF 1). Fact-table authoring is a feature, not a key rename.

export: { [ -d node_modules ] || npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --loglevel=error >/dev/null; } && npx --yes tsx conformance/export.ts

unsupported.type_crud: the SDK ships no CRUD generation at all — `grep -rn crud sdks/official/fraiseql-go` matches nothing, and its builders expose no flag for it. Nine of the eleven SDKs have a generator; adding a tenth is a feature, not a key rename, so the gap is declared rather than papered over (#1182).

unsupported.fact_tables: the SDK has no fact-table authoring surface — its only `fact_table` matches are the mutation key `invalidates_fact_tables` (AF 1). Fact-table authoring is a feature, not a key rename.
unsupported.field_localized: the SDK has no `localized` field authoring yet (#1513 shipped it in the Python and TypeScript SDKs first); tracked in #1527.
unsupported.mutation_argument_localized: the SDK has no `localized` argument authoring yet (#1513 shipped it in the Python and TypeScript SDKs first); tracked in #1527.

unsupported.fact_tables: the SDK authors no fact table: `@GraphQLFactTable` registers the annotated class as an ordinary type and emits no `fact_tables` entry, so there is no table to link to its type (AF 1). Fact-table authoring is a feature, not a key rename.

unsupported.subscriptions: the SDK ships no subscription authoring surface at all — no builder, no decorator, no registry entry. Five of the eleven SDKs have one (Python, TypeScript, Go, PHP, Java); adding a sixth is a feature, not a key rename, so the gap is declared rather than papered over (#1024).
